in.other_title: Self-play debate training improves LLM judge accuracy; consultancy training does not
in.rationale: Kenton et al. name training debaters and consultants on the judge's signal as the most immediate future work. Arnesen et al. train with self-play and report judge accuracy rises with debate training but not with consultancy training; the judges are language-model based evaluators.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether training debaters and consultants on a judge's signal raises judge accuracy, on a long-context reading comprehension task with language-model judges

text: The authors give as the most immediate future work training debater and consultant models on the judge's signal, hoping to see both judge accuracy and debater skill improve, and also list human judges, other weak-strong asymmetries (tool use, code execution, modality access), debate with cross-examination, iterated amplification, behaviour under easy-to-hard distribution shift, and robustness to misaligned models.
title: Does training debaters and consultants on weak-judge signals improve judge accuracy?
